title: A Bakery for the Orchard
premise: Rosalind Brightwater has spent ten years ghostwriting a famous rival's memoirs while secretly exchanging anonymous letters with a stranger who once answered her ad in a literary magazine. When her letter-writer, Elias Thorne, moves in next door to open an orchard bakery, she recognizes his handwriting instantly but hides her identity, terrified he'll learn she's been the invisible hand behind his rival's bestselling book. As their friendship deepens into love, Rosalind's contract demands she finish the memoir by spring, forcing her to choose between the career that kept her fed and the man who made her feel seen. At the memoir's launch party, she confesses everything publicly; Elias, hurt but having suspected, chooses her anyway, and together they build a life where the bakery and her own name share one sign.
about_author: Gideon Kavanagh is the pen name of a former pastry chef who traded early mornings at the oven for late nights at the keyboard. He writes love stories set in small towns where food is a language and second chances rise like bread.

chapters.title: The Handwriting on the Wall
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Moving day next door: crates stamped with an orchard logo, and a man whose handwriting on a delivery slip stops her cold—the same slanted capitals that have signed ten years of letters. She retreats inside, heart pounding. Emotional beat: recognition and fear colliding; the past has literally moved in.

chapters.title: Flour and Anonymity
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He opens Thorne & Orchard Bakery, unaware his new neighbor is the woman behind 'R.B., Box 44.' He bakes her a welcome loaf; she invents a fake name, 'Rosie Winters,' to accept it. Emotional beat: warm comedy masking dread—every kindness deepens her deception.

chapters.title: Terms of the Contract
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Her publisher, Marguerite Voss, tightens the deadline: rival author Celeste Marchand's memoir must be finished in four months for a spring launch. Rosalind realizes the launch will fall in the same town square as Elias's grand opening. Emotional beat: claustrophobia—the trap of duty drawing shut.

chapters.title: Letters, Unsent
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Through flashbacks we see how the correspondence began: her grief after her mother's death, his reply from a hospital bed. Now they talk across the fence about everything except their secret selves. Emotional beat: intimacy built on omission; found family begins with his orphaned niece, Juniper.

chapters.title: Juniper's Orchard
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Juniper, eight, adopts Rosie as family, dragging both adults into apple-picking and Sunday pancakes. Rosalind feels the first crack in her invisibility—she wants to be real to this child. Emotional beat: belonging as temptation; the price of survival starts feeling too high.

chapters.title: Celeste's Version
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Celeste arrives to review chapters and casually reveals she knows a 'ghost named Brightwater' exists—and wants her fired if identified. Meanwhile Elias mentions his pen pal for the first time, wistful. Emotional beat: jealousy of herself; two lives pressing toward collision.

chapters.title: The Almost-Confession
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A storm knocks out power; by candlelight Elias nearly tells Rosie about his letters, showing her one unsent draft addressed to R.B. Rosalind almost speaks, then flees to meet Celeste's deadline instead. Emotional beat: cowardice and longing; the reader sees how close rescue was.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She delivers the finished memoir, hollowed out, and finds Elias reading a copy of Celeste's previous book—acknowledging 'with gratitude to my ghost.' His face when he connects the initials. Emotional beat: exposure without words; betrayal assumed before truth can be spoken.

chapters.title: Launch Day
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The memoir launches in the square beside his opening. Rosalind takes the microphone, names herself, and reads aloud the letter that started it all. Silence, then Juniper claps. Elias walks through the crowd—not to Celeste's table, but to her. Emotional beat: climax; choosing risk over safety in public.

chapters.title: A Bakery for the Orchard
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Spring: they repaint the shop sign to read 'Thorne & Brightwater,' and Rosalind begins her own book under her own name. Juniper plants an apple tree between the houses. Emotional beat: resolution—love against duty resolved not by abandoning work, but by claiming authorship of her own life.
